openings.claim: Does the incumbent clamp have an achievable preload that satisfies both retention and gloved service time?
openings.delta: Keep the bolted strips and cork carrier; change the evidential dependency from assumed screw preload to paired displacement and service measurements at recorded screw settings. No replacement is established.
openings.prediction: The nearest rival explanation is that preload sufficient for retention makes screwdriver release and return too slow. Low displacement with service above sixty seconds supports that rival; compliant displacement and service together weaken it. The magnet pull difference does not predict cork friction or clamp performance on the spare.
openings.probe: Check M4 slot fit, compliant placement and screwdriver access before drilling strips. If possible, fabricate one configuration within eighty minutes using supplied parts. Within twenty observation minutes, conduct at most three twenty-stroke runs and three paired removal/return checks; record screw settings, displacement and timing. Use the spare for the final run and thick gloves for its removal; handle only unmarked regions. Failure above 1 mm or sixty seconds defeats the tested setting. No accessible compliant placement defeats this configuration; exhausted time leaves untested settings unresolved.
assumptions: Slot dimensions, strip stiffness and screwdriver access permit assembly.
Recorded settings reproduce adequate preload despite cork compression and plate substitution.
Available observation time permits informative paired checks.

assessment: This critiques two dependencies of the same clamp, without adding equipment or permitting constraint relaxation. Passing one setting is bounded probe evidence, not deployment or proof of unspecified-load reliability.

lineage.reason: Preserve the clamp while making its coupled retention/service feasibility an explicit unresolved test.

attacks.dependency: Achievable screw preload resists strokes on either plate; magnet-release evidence cannot establish mechanical substitution insensitivity.
The retaining setting allows accessible screwdriver release and gloved return within sixty seconds; slot presence establishes neither access nor timing.
